The concept of a common time was primarily developed by various African cultures and can be observed alongside 2/4 and 6/8 in many rhythms and beats that originate from their traditions. Consequently, many other cultures do not utilize this concept. Music from South Asia often lacks a fixed rhythm as understood in Western contexts, instead featuring a pattern for performance (if I recall correctly from my experience with traditional percussion). Indigenous peoples from certain regions of North America, particularly in the south and west, often employed timekeeping similar to 5/4 but were also known to vary it.
